=== CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19959-19962 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: The user-authored `grouped_items[].title` in the PERSIST_ORCH_GROUP_DIAG_JSON jq filter only has control characters, `<!--` and `-->` removed. It is neither marked untrusted nor cleaned of `===` runs or embedded instructions, and it reaches the stall-judge prompt (20242-20245, 20277-20279).
  WHY: A crafted title such as `=== STALL JUDGE TASK ===`, or one carrying instructions, can imitate the prompt's section headers and steer the judge's automated recovery action. minimax and luna rated this MAJOR and gemini gave no severity, so the highest (MAJOR→high) is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disagreed: it checked and did not report this, saying existing diagnostics already carry author text with no fence. It listed `gsub("={3,}"; "= = =")` only as a hardening change.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:457-471 | severity=high | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: In `group_failures`, an item that is active, has no journal and still carries a stale `persist_group_released_key` is added to neither `blocked` nor `clear`/`clear_cooldown`, so the field stays in state forever.
  WHY: gemini says the stale field could block future grouping. minimax says it has no functional effect when `key is None`, but the state comment keeps carrying it. minimax rated this MAJOR and gemini gave no severity, so the highest (MAJOR→high) is used. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disagreed: it checked and did not report this, saying a None key cannot join a bucket and the field is cleared once a journal appears.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19968-19977 | severity=low | confidence=5
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5, google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3, openai_gpt-6-luna]
  PROBLEM: In `persist_orch_group_failures`, the duplicate-post marker `AI_PERSIST_GROUPED_V1 key=<k> owner=<n>` has no grouping-episode identity. A comment from an earlier episode (fetched through `comments(last: 100)`, line 20711) therefore stops the comment from being posted when the item is grouped again under the same key and owner.
  WHY: After a `key_changed`, `owner_key_changed` or `journal_absent` release followed by regrouping on the same key and owner, the item is paused with no explanation. That contradicts plan P8 step 2 ("post one comment per item when it is grouped"). Rated NIT by sonnet, minimax and luna; gemini gave no severity.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19968-19974 | severity=low | confidence=4
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite, minimax_minimax-m3]
  PROBLEM: The duplicate-post check compares `.user.login` with `PERSIST_JOURNAL_LOGIN_CACHE` by exact string equality. The REST login from `gh api user` and the GraphQL `author { login }` may differ in case or in the `[bot]` suffix.
  WHY: If they differ, the marker never matches, so after a failed `post_state_comment` the pause comment is posted again on the next tick. The fix is to normalise both sides as `attempt_journal._norm_login` does. minimax rated this NIT and gemini gave no severity. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disagreed: it checked and found that both sources return the same login and case, and that `[bot]` identities cannot reach this point.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:group_failures | severity=low | confidence=2
  flagged_by: [anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5]
  PROBLEM: The owner `prior` set is built only from bucket members. When the only members that recorded the existing owner are held (their cache entry is missing), the recorded owner is ignored and the owner is chosen again by `min(members, key=lambda g: (items[g]["earliest"], g))`.
  WHY: One transient cache gap can flip the owner twice (11 -> 10 -> 12 and then back) and post extra "## Paused" comments, which is the flapping the hold was meant to stop. Fix: also take `prior` candidates from held items whose `old_group(g)["key"] == key`. Rated NIT.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19888, 19934, 19941 | severity=low | confidence=3
  flagged_by: [google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite]
  PROBLEM: Cleanup of the `pog_details` and `pog_out` scratch files is spread across several error paths.
  WHY: A future error path could miss a cleanup call and leak scratch files in `RUNTIME_DIR` (or `/tmp`). The source gave no severity, so low is assumed. anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 disagreed: it checked that every exit path after `mktemp` removes `pog_details`, `pog_out` and `pog_tmp`.
=== END CONSENSUS FINDINGS ===

=== CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===
(No task gaps reported.)
=== END CONSENSUS TASK GAPS ===

=== FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:group_failures (`held` set; `prior = sorted({o for o in (_positive_int((old_group(g) or {}).get("owner")) for g in members if ...) if o in members})`) | severity=NIT | confidence=2
  PROBLEM: `prior` is built only from bucket members, so when the members that recorded the owner are held for a tick, that owner is ignored and the owner is chosen again by earliest entry.
  WHY: A transient cache gap flips the owner twice (11 -> 10 -> 12, then back to 10) and posts extra comments, which is the flapping the hold was meant to stop. Fix: take `prior` from held items whose `old_group(g)["key"] == key` (about 2 lines).
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:persist_orch_group_failures, duplicate-post check `--arg m "AI_PERSIST_GROUPED_V1 key=${pog_key} owner=${pog_owner} "` against `comments(last: 100)` (line 20711) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The marker matches on (key, owner) only and has no episode identity, so an older comment from a released grouping stops the post.
  WHY: Regrouping after a `key_changed`, `owner_key_changed` or `journal_absent` release pauses the item with no explanation, which contradicts plan P8 step 2. Fix: skip only when the marker comment's `created_at` is newer than the newest journal entry, or document the gap in the fragment.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh persist_orch_group_failures `title:` jq expression. Add `| gsub("={3,}"; "= = =")` before `.[0:120]` so titles made of `===` runs cannot imitate prompt section headers (1 line).
- HARDENING: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py group_failures unknown-hold branch `cooldown[gh] = old["key"]`. Set it only when `_HEX12_RE.match(old["key"])`, otherwise use reason `field_invalid` (3 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- NOTE: Checked and not reported (4 related items):
  - The title reaching the judge without an untrusted marker (19959-19960, 20242-20245). `recent_tracking_comments` (20036-20044) already exposes author text there.
  - The gemini `clear_cooldown` stale field.
  - The gemini scattered-cleanup point.
  - Login normalisation.
  The pass-1 TASK_GAP about validating hour values in the shell was rejected. CI: copilot-pull-request-reviewer failed with `custom_instructions_too_large` (HTTP 422), and nine checks were still running (collection_status=timeout).
=== END FINDINGS FROM anthropic_claude-sonnet-5_5 ===

=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19961-19962 (within PERSIST_ORCH_GROUP_DIAG_JSON jq filter) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: User-authored titles reach the stall-judge prompt and the posted comment without enough sanitisation.
  WHY: Only `<!--`, `-->` and control characters are removed. `===` is not neutralised, so section-header-like text can be injected and may influence stall recovery.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:457-463 (within group_failures) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The logic that clears `persist_group_released_key` through `clear_cooldown` does not cover all cases.
  WHY: An active item with no trusted journal and a stale key that does not match is added to neither `clear_cooldown` nor `clear`. The field persists and may block future grouping.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19968-19973 (within persist_orch_group_failures duplicate-post check) | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The existing-comment check suppresses the comment for every future grouping episode with the same key and owner.
  WHY: The static marker `AI_PERSIST_GROUPED_V1 key=<key> owner=<n>` has no episode identifier or timestamp, so regroupings after a release get no explanatory comment.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19968-19973 (within persist_orch_group_failures duplicate-post check) | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The login comparison uses exact string equality.
  WHY: `PERSIST_JOURNAL_LOGIN_CACHE` may differ from `.user.login?` in case or in the `[bot]` suffix. The check then misses the comment, and the pause comment is posted again every tick after a failed `post_state_comment`.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19888, 19934, 19941 | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: Cleanup of the `pog_details` and `pog_out` scratch files is spread across error paths.
  WHY: A new error path could easily miss a cleanup call and leak scratch files in `RUNTIME_DIR` (or `/tmp`).

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19959-19960 (the `title:` filter in `PERSIST_ORCH_GROUP_DIAG_JSON`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The title filter strips only `\p{Cc}|\p{Zl}|\p{Zp}`, `<!--` and `-->`, not `===` runs. The title reaches the judge prompt (20242-20245, after the header at 20277-20279) and the SEmble query (line 20258). The rule `_FENCE_FORGERY_RE` in scripts/attempt_journal.py:260 is not applied.
  WHY: A user-authored title reaches the LLM as if it were a prompt header.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19971-19974 (the duplicate-post `jq -e` check) | severity=NIT | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: The check compares `.user.login` with `PERSIST_JOURNAL_LOGIN_CACHE` exactly. The REST `gh api user --jq .login` (line 19875) keeps `[bot]`, while GraphQL `author { login }` (line 20774) strips it. The regex at 19876 accepts both. `_norm_login` (scripts/attempt_journal.py:176-182) should be applied to both sides.
  WHY: For a bot identity the marker never matches, so a failed `post_state_comment` leads to a duplicate pause comment.
- scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:465-471 (the `persist_group_released_key` loop in `group_failures`) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=4
  PROBLEM: An item that is active, has no journal and has `key != released_key` falls through both the `blocked` and `clear` branches, so the stale field stays forever. It has no functional effect when `key is None`.
  WHY: A paused item whose cache entry is emptied (cache reset to `{}`, or a `comments_available: false` batch) keeps the field, and the state diff shows it indefinitely.
- scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19971-19977 (marker check at 19971-19974, marker at 19977) | severity=NIT | confidence=3
  PROBLEM: The marker holds only `key=<k> owner=<n>` with no episode identifier. When an item is regrouped after a `key_changed` release, the cached comment matches and the new comment is skipped.
  WHY: The item is paused again without a fresh explanation, which contradicts plan P8 step 2.
- HARDENING: scripts/persist_orchestrator.py:467. Check `_HEX12_RE.match(...)` before `blocked.add(gh)`, otherwise release as `field_invalid` (2 lines). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 1.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19971-19974. Normalise the login on both sides with `ascii_downcase | sub("\\[bot\\]$"; "")` (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 2.
- HARDENING: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:19959-19960. Append `| gsub("={3,}"; "= =")` after the `<!--|-->` strip (1 line). HARDENING_RISK_SCORE: 3.
=== END FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
